```po_plan
  {"option_id": "B", "label": "Emergency PO of 163 units to Uppababy Pacific", "transfer_units": 0, "po_units": 163, "first_stock_date": "2026-07-10", "stockout_days": 29, "lost_sales_aud": 87506, "transfer_cost_aud": 0, "stock_value_aud": 141713, "cover_after_weeks": 8, "lifts_shortage": false, "guardrails": []},
  {"option_id": "C", "label": "Expedited PO of 124 units via 3PL (18 days)", "transfer_units": 0, "po_units": 124, "first_stock_date": "2026-06-30", "stockout_days": 19, "lost_sales_aud": 57332, "transfer_cost_aud": 12937, "stock_value_aud": 107806, "cover_after_weeks": 6.6, "lifts_shortage": false,

 "recommended": "C",

```

### What is happening
- The tool picked **Double Stroller at the NSW DC** because it has the most stores out: 8 of 17 stores in NSW and ACT, including Chatswood, Wollongong, Penrith, Sydney CBD and Canberra.
- The region has **2 weeks of cover** against a 4-week target and is losing **AUD 21.1K of sales a week**.
- **The supplier is not the cause.** Uppababy Pacific has filled 100% of NSW Double Stroller orders since 1 May. Its weekly on-time-in-full rate is 88.8–94.8%. The data has no fill rate for before 1 May, no short-shipped orders and no open orders. So the gap looks like orders that were too small for demand, not shipments that came up short.
- Odd wording: the tool's do-nothing note says the next order "would land short again," which contradicts the 100% fill rate. I've ignored that line.
- **Every DC is short too** (1.6–2.6 weeks of cover), so no DC has stock to spare.
- **No campaigns are affected.**

### The options
| | First stock | Stockout days | Lost sales | Extra cost | PO stock value | Cover after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Do nothing | 7 Aug | 57 | AUD 172.0K | – | – | – |
| A: transfer from VIC | none | 57 | AUD 172.0K | AUD 0 | – | 2 wks (**BLOCKED**) |
| B: emergency PO, 163 units | 10 Jul | 29 | AUD 87.5K | AUD 0 | AUD 141.7K | 8 wks |
| C: expedited PO, 124 units (18 days) | 30 Jun | 19 | AUD 57.3K | AUD 12.9K premium | AUD 107.8K | 6.6 wks |



### Recommendation
**Option C.**
- **Why C:** both B and C bring cover back to the 4-week target and last until the next regular supply. C gets stock in 10 days sooner. That saves about AUD 30K more in sales than B, for an expedite premium of AUD 12.9K (an assumed 12% of stock value).
- **Transfer only (A):** this isn't possible. Moving stock would push VIC or any other DC below its 3-week floor. NSW would stay at 2 weeks of cover, fully exposed.
- **Risk on the POs:** at the recent 100% fill rate, the risk is low. But weekly on-time-in-full has dipped as low as 88.8%, so either order could arrive a little late or short.
- **Wider shortage:** the whole network is short, so the other DCs may need their own recovery plans.

### What approval does
No campaign is blocked, so nothing gets unblocked. Option C lands after 19 days, not within 7, so the 8 stores stay SHORT until about 30 June.

This plan is a **draft** (RCV-11170327237). A supply planner needs to approve one option on the Stockout recovery page.
